events.title: Trouble at School
events.text: {person:child} has been coming home quiet. Today you learned why: someone at school has been picking on them.

choices.label: Go to the school and sort it out
choices.outcome_text: It was awkward, official, and absolutely the right call.

choices.label: Coach them to stand up for themselves
choices.outcome_text: I coached my kid to stand up to the bully, practising comebacks at the dinner table.

choices.label: Kids work these things out alone
choices.outcome_text: The quiet at dinner lasted a long time.

events.title: Science Fair Season
events.text: The science fair is in two weeks and {person:child} wants to build a volcano. A big volcano.

choices.label: Buy proper supplies
choices.outcome_text: The eruption made the neighbours look over the fence.

choices.label: Build it from cupboard scraps together
choices.outcome_text: It leaned a little, and it was magnificent.

choices.label: Let them handle it alone
choices.outcome_text: The volcano was small. So was the smile about it.

events.title: Team Tryouts
events.text: {person:child} wants to join the school team. Practices are three evenings a week, plus fees.

choices.label: Pay the fees and clear your evenings
choices.outcome_text: I memorised the practice schedule faster than they did.

choices.label: Make the logistics work yourself
choices.outcome_text: My weeks became a relay race of pickups.

choices.label: It's too much this term
choices.outcome_text: They said fine. They did not say it warmly.

events.title: The Report Card
events.text: {person:child}'s report card came home with numbers that need a conversation.

choices.label: Hire a tutor
choices.outcome_text: The next report card told its own story.

choices.label: Ground them until it improves
choices.outcome_text: The house was disciplined and cold.

choices.label: Grades aren't everything
choices.outcome_text: I told myself grades are not everything, and the real conversation with my kid never quite happened.

events.title: Lunch Money
events.text: {person:child} admits, eventually, that lunch money has been 'going missing' at school.

choices.label: Top up the money and talk about it
choices.outcome_text: The real conversation happened over dinner.

choices.label: Pack lunch from now on
choices.outcome_text: I packed my kid's lunch from then on: balanced meals and slightly resentful gratitude.

choices.label: They should handle it themselves
choices.outcome_text: I made my kid handle the lunch money alone, and they stopped mentioning lunch entirely.

events.title: Please Please Please
events.text: {person:child} has produced a hand-drawn contract promising to walk, feed and love a dog. It is very convincing.

choices.label: Adopt the dog
choices.outcome_text: The contract survived three weeks. The dog stayed forever.

choices.label: Start with a fish
choices.outcome_text: The fish was named Captain. Responsibilities were partial.

choices.label: No pets
choices.outcome_text: The drawings on the fridge stopped appearing.
